Department: Department of Computing Sciences

College: College of Informatics and Computing Sciences

Campus: ARASOF-Nasugbu

VI. Cooperating Agency: (if any) Municipality of Nasugbu

VII. Executive Brief:

This project develops a community-led coastal monitoring system.
It combines field observation and local knowledge.

VIII. Rationale: (include available statistics related to the problem)

Coastal communities require timely, reliable environmental information for local decisions.

IX. Objectives of the Project:

Specific Objectives:

  1. Establish a baseline coastal profile.

  2. Develop and validate the monitoring workflow.

X. Expected Output of the Project: (based on expanded 6Ps & 2Is of research)

  1. Publication: One peer-reviewed journal article
  2. Product: Coastal monitoring dashboard
  3. People Service: Training for community monitors
  4. Place & Partnership: University-LGU partnership
  5. Policy: Local monitoring protocol
  6. Social Impact: Improved community participation
  7. Economic Impact: Reduced monitoring costs

XI. Review of Related Literature: (minimum of ten literature/studies reviewed)

Community coastal monitoring benefits from an integrated local research approach.

Recent coastal monitoring studies demonstrate the value of participatory data collection.

XII. Methodology:

  • Research Design

    The study uses a sequential mixed-method research design.

  • Specific Method to obtain the objectives

    A. Community field research
    1. Researchers will conduct surveys, interviews, and coastal transect observations.

  • Data Analysis

    Quantitative results will use descriptive statistics and qualitative data will use thematic analysis.

XIII. Duties and Responsibilities of each member:

Project Leader: FACULTY PROJECT LEADER (60%)

Leads the project, assures research quality, and coordinates reporting.

Project Staff (s): RESEARCH STAFF MEMBER (40%)

Coordinates field data collection and prepares the validated dataset.
